title: Interregion Commit Coordinator and Granular Burst Signal Fanout
author: Anika Bose
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets that span regions were occasionally double-allocating burst credits and emitting duplicate utilization spikes when tenant requests were shifted by global load-balancers. This led to transient SLA overshoots and noisy telemetry across regions. Motivation: provide a lightweight cross-region commit coordination mechanism and a fanout adapter for burst signals so autoscalers and ledgers see a single authoritative event stream per logical surge. What this PR does: (1) introduces a Commit Coordinator controller that reconciles 'provision intents' across regional controllers using a compact lease protocol (gossip + tombstones) and a per-tenant commit horizon to avoid racey double-commits; (2) adds a Granular Burst Signal Fanout layer that deduplicates and annotates burst events with origin region, sequence, and sanity TTL before writing to the utilization pipeline; (3) instruments new telemetry hooks and tracing spans to show cross-region reconciliation latency and de-duplication ratios; (4) adds an operator command (redwoodctl provision commit-status) to inspect commit horizon for a tenant and force-safe-rewind for legacy reservoirs. Design notes: the coordinator is intentionally conservative — it serializes commit windows at 1s granularity to preserve correctness while letting local pools maintain low-latency admits for steady state. The fanout performs idempotency checks using sequence+origin and guards the ledger using a short-lived consensus token (not full Raft). We favored an eventual-consistent reconciliation with fast local admits plus a graceful revoke path rather than strong synchronous global locks to avoid latency regressions. Migration/rollout: feature-gated via cluster config (ENABLE_INTERREGION_COMMIT_COORDINATOR). Default is off; rollout plan is: canary in single interregion tenant pool, observe dedup ratio and commit lag, then enable by regions. Backwards compatibility: coordinator tolerates older regional controllers — they will continue emitting events and coordinator will reconcile without requiring immediate upgrades. Testing: unit tests for dedupe logic, integration E2E across two-region kind clusters, load soak verifying no >2% additional latency in the steady path, synthetic chaos test that flips region leadership. Related: references ENG-1942 for rollout plan and SRE-23 for runbook updates.
commits: 6 commits: 1) initial coordinator scaffold and lease protocol, 2) fanout adapter and idempotency key implementation, 3) telemetry + tracing spans, 4) redwoodctl command and e2e fixture, 5) k8s manifests and feature gate wiring, 6) docs and runbook addition
discussion: Marcus: Can we avoid another cross-region RPC in the hot path? Author: The hot path remains local admits; the coordinator runs async and reconciles within the commit horizon. Only the fast revoke path will incur an interregion call and that is gated. Diego: What about clock skew across regions affecting sequence TTL? Author: We use monotonic sequence per origin and include a TTL window of 5s with wall-clock tolerant checks; tests simulate 2s skew. Priya: Add a metric for 'dedupe_ratio' and an alert threshold. Author: Added metric and SLO proposal in SRE-23. Marcus: Please add stronger unit tests around tombstone expiry. Author: Added two unit tests and an integration chaos test. Diego: CI flaked on e2e; reran and passed. Final: Approved by Marcus and Diego after addressing tests.

release_notes:
- New: Interregion Commit Coordinator to prevent burst double-allocation in multi-region fleets.
- New: Granular Burst Signal Fanout reduces duplicate telemetry across regions and exposes dedupe_ratio metric.
- Ops: redwoodctl provision commit-status command for inspecting commit horizons.
Rollout: feature-gated. See docs/runbooks/interregion-commit-coordinator.md for rollout steps and runbook.
